group_mark.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "Numerals of more than four digits are divided by spaces (or by dots), in groups of three"; ICU 78 (CLDR 48) formats 1234567.89 in hu as "1 234 567,89"

decimal_mark.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "The beginning of decimal fractions is marked with a comma."; "The integer part of a decimal is divided from the rest by a comma (e.g. 3,14 '3.14')"; ICU 78 (CLDR 48) formats 1234567.89 in hu as "1 234 567,89"

space_groups.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "Numbers written in digits can be written without a space up to four digits; above that, they are divided by spaces from the end by the usual three-digit division"

scale_noun_agrees.source: Wiktionary, "három" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-három.wikitext): "Három könyvet vettem.|I bought three books."; the noun after a count keeps one form for every count, so 'egymillió' and 'kétmillió' use the same scale word.

plural_scale_needs_count.source: Hungarian scale words have no plural form after a count ('kétmillió'); the setting matters for no entry.

joiner_before_round_hundred.source: No joiner stands after the thousands (joiner_between_groups is never): CLDR 48 RBNF hu %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1500: "ezerötszáz"; CLDR 48 RBNF hu %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1020: "ezerhúsz".

small_multiplier_starts_group.source: unicode-rbnf 2.4.1 (CLDR RBNF hu data), %spellout-cardinal, rendering of 1100 and 2010: "ezerszáz", "kétezertíz": the hundred or ten after the thousands is the next group, so a hundred or ten multiplier counts no group of thousands.

comma_between_classes.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography": "they should be divided by hyphens by the usual three-digit division over 2000 (e.g. kétezer-egy '2,001')": a hyphen, not a comma, stands between two classes. No source opened shows a comma there, so a comma ends a number.

joiner_before_last_group.source: CLDR 48 RBNF hu %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 1020: "ezerhúsz"; Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography": "kétezer-egy '2,001'": no conjunction stands before the last group.

ordinal_style.source: Hungarian ordinals are entries with 'ordinal': true; only the last element is ordinal ('huszonötödik', CLDR 48 RBNF hu %spellout-ordinal, ICU 78 rendering of 25: "huszonötödik").

compound_words.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "If cardinal numbers are written in letters, they should be written as one word up to 2000 (e.g. ezerkilencszázkilencvenkilenc '1,999')"; "they should be divided by hyphens by the usual three-digit division over 2000 (e.g. kétezer-egy '2,001')"

inflection_position.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "Words containing a suffixed numeral are written as one word (e.g. húszméteres út"; a case ending goes on the last element of a number ('kétezer-ötszázat').

fraction_agreement.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "If a fraction functions as a noun, the quantifier is written separately (e.g. egy negyed 'one quarter')"; Wiktionary, "három" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-három.wikitext): "Három könyvet vettem.|I bought three books.": a noun after a numeral keeps the singular, so 'két harmad' has no plural form.

glued_denominators.source: Wiktionary, Module:number list/data/hu (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/follow-up-prs/hu-denominators/render/number-list-data-hu.lua): numbers[200] has "cardinal = {"kétszáz", "kettőszáz<tag:formal>"}" and "fractional = "kétszázad"", and numbers[10000] has "fractional = "tízezred"": the part word of 200 is the count glued to the part word of 100, as the cardinal glues it to the scale word, so the glued count multiplies the part word. AkH 12 §293 (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/follow-up-prs/hu-denominators/render/akh12-293.txt): "Ha azonban a tőszámnévi jelzős törtszámnév egészében jelzői szerepű, a két számnevet egybeírjuk, például: az ország kétharmad része, háromnegyed óra múlva": before a noun the glued form can also be a count of parts ("háromszázad másodperc" as 3/100). hu.wikipedia uses the lone glued form as a multiplier (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/follow-up-prs/hu-denominators/render/hu-Bróm.wikitext: "háromszázad része a klórénak"; hu-Oxigén.wikitext: "kétezred részét"; hu-Atommag.wikitext: "tízezred része"; hu-Izotópos_összetétel.wikitext: "százezred Å-nyi (1 fm)"; hu-ETME.wikitext: "háromezred részével"), so a glued part word of a hundred or more with no count before it reads as one part of the product ("háromszázad" is 1/300) at the homograph confidence, and 3/100 stays the alternative.

decimal_fraction.source: Wiktionary, "egész" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-egész.wikitext): "Names the integer part of a decimal fraction, when it is spoken out loud."; "nem kettő, hanem egy '''egész''' hét tized"; the digits after the point are a count of tenths, hundredths or thousandths ('tized', 'század', 'ezred').

dot_ordinal.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "Ordinal numbers written in digits take a full stop (e.g. 3. sor '3rd line')"

joiner.source: 'és' (and) joins a half to a number ('két és fél'); no conjunction joins the parts of a number (Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "If cardinal numbers are written in letters, they should be written as one word up to 2000 (e.g. ezerkilencszázkilencvenkilenc '1,999')"; "they should be divided by hyphens by the usual three-digit division over 2000 (e.g. kétezer-egy '2,001')").

decimal_marker.source: CLDR 48 RBNF hu %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of 2.5: "kettő egész öt"; Wiktionary, "egész" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-egész.wikitext): "Names the integer part of a decimal fraction, when it is spoken out loud."

minus.source: CLDR 48 RBNF hu %spellout-cardinal, ICU 78 rendering of -5: "mínusz öt"; 'minusz' is the spelling without the accent.

minus_idioms.source: No Hungarian idiom puts 'mínusz' before a positive number.

number_name.source: hu.wiktionary, "one and all" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/follow-up-prs/hu/render/hu-one_and_all.raw): "#[[mindenki kivétel nélkül]], [[egytől egyig]]": the idiom means everyone without exception and counts nothing.

noun_after_count.source: Wiktionary, "hét", Hungarian: Numeral "seven", Noun "week", with the example "Egy hét hét napból áll." ("One week consists of seven days."). Wikipedia, "Hungarian noun phrase": "Therefore, the plural is not used with numerals or quantity expressions." A count before "hét" counts the singular noun: "öt hét" is five weeks, and no Hungarian number puts "hét" after another count.

article_one.source: Wiktionary, "egy" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-egy.wikitext): "{{senseid|hu|a}} [[a]], [[an]] {{gloss|indefinite article}}"; "egy csepp a tengerben|a drop in the ocean"

of.source: Hungarian has no word that multiplies a scale word.

fraction_of.source: Hungarian puts no word between a fraction and a collective.

denominator_particle.source: Hungarian has no particle like Portuguese 'avos'.

class_noun.source: Hungarian has no class noun after a collective.

half_unit.source: Hungarian puts 'fél' before the unit ('fél kiló').

abbreviation.source: No Hungarian number word is also an abbreviation with a period.

lone_decimal_mark.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "The beginning of decimal fractions is marked with a comma."; "The integer part of a decimal is divided from the rest by a comma (e.g. 3,14 '3.14')"; so ',5' is 0.5.

range_cue.source: Wiktionary, "között" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-range-között.wikitext): "{{head|hu|postposition}}"; "# [[between]], [[among]]"; 'között' stands after the numbers ('kettő és öt között'), so no word before a range opens it.

digit_suffix_mark.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "The full stop is retained even before the hyphen that connects suffixes (e.g. a 10.-kel 'with the 10th')"; "digits, punctuation marks, typographical signs, abbreviations, and acronyms take a hyphen before suffixes"; the suffix after the hyphen is no number word.

date_month.source: Wikipedia, "Hungarian orthography" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikipedia-Hungarian_orthography.wikitext): "Ordinal numbers written in digits take a full stop (e.g. 3. sor '3rd line'). The full stop is retained even before the hyphen that connects suffixes (e.g. a 10.-kel 'with the 10th'). Dates are an exception to this rule, see below."; "The year is always given in Arabic numerals and it is followed by a full stop. The name of the month can be written in full or abbreviated, or it can be marked with a Roman or Arabic numeral."; Wiktionary, "január" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-január.wikitext): "abr=jan."; Wiktionary, "február" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-február.wikitext): "abr=febr."; Wiktionary, "március" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-március.wikitext): "abr=márc."; Wiktionary, "április" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-április.wikitext): "abr=ápr."; Wiktionary, "május" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-május.wikitext): "abr=máj."; Wiktionary, "június" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-június.wikitext): "abr=jún."; Wiktionary, "július" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-július.wikitext): "abr=júl."; Wiktionary, "augusztus" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-augusztus.wikitext): "abr=aug."; Wiktionary, "szeptember" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-szeptember.wikitext): "abr=szept."; Wiktionary, "október" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-október.wikitext): "abr=okt."; Wiktionary, "november" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-november.wikitext): "abr=nov."; Wiktionary, "december" (knowledge/wiki/audits/numtag/lang-ports/uralic-turkic/sources/wikt-hu-december.wikitext): "abr=dec."; after a year and its full stop comes a month, so a full stop before a month name is no ordinal mark.
